1	/**
2	 * What the canvas draws, written by hand rather than generated.
3	 *
4	 * This is the browser's own view of one world — a map with its numbers filled
5	 * in — and it is deliberately **not** taken from `src/api/schema.ts`. That file
6	 * is generated from the server's description of itself, and the routes that
7	 * serve a computed world are being written at the same time as this canvas. If
8	 * the canvas typed itself against those routes it could not be built until they
9	 * existed, and it would have to be rewritten every time they changed shape.
10	 *
11	 * The rule that shapes everything below: **every slot where a likelihood would
12	 * go is optional.** A number nobody has computed is not a zero and not a blank;
13	 * it is an absence, and an absence carries the reason it is absent — "no
14	 * market", "no engine yet", or a dash inviting the reader's own number. That is
15	 * the whole of the traceability rule as it reaches this layer: nothing on
16	 * screen may be a number nobody can account for.
17	 *
18	 * Nothing in this file, or anywhere under `src/world`, does arithmetic on a
19	 * likelihood. Numbers arrive from the server and are carried, unchanged and at
20	 * full precision, to the moment they are printed.
21	 *
22	 * **One thing here is taken from the generated description after all, and it is
23	 * the exception that proves the rule:** a branch, in the shape the server writes
24	 * one. That shape is not a view of anything — it is what travels back over the
25	 * wire when a world is asked for — so re-stating it by hand would be writing
26	 * down the server's own words and waiting for them to drift.
27	 */
28	
29	import type { components } from "../api/schema";
30	
31	/** What a claim is for. Its shape on the canvas carries this, never its colour. */
32	export type ClaimKind = "hypothesis" | "event" | "market" | "not_tradeable";
33	
34	/**
35	 * How a push behaves when its cause goes away. `trigger` is a toppled domino —
36	 * it stays toppled. `sustain` is an apple on a desk — take the desk away and
37	 * the apple falls.
38	 */
39	export type LinkMode = "trigger" | "sustain";
40	
41	/** Whose number this is. The three are never averaged into one. */
42	export type BeliefOwner = "model" | "user" | "market";
43	
44	/**
45	 * A likelihood and the range around it, both at full precision.
46	 *
47	 * The range says **how sure we are of the number** — not how much the world can
48	 * move. How much the world can move is already inside `p`. Rounding to two
49	 * significant figures happens once, at the moment of display, and never here.
50	 */
51	export interface Ranged {
52	  /** How likely the claim is to come out true, from 0 to 1. */
53	  readonly p: number;
54	  /** The bottom of the range around `p`. Never above it. */
55	  readonly lo: number;
56	  /** The top of the range around `p`. Never below it. */
57	  readonly hi: number;
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Which of the four absences this is. It is what picks the words.
62	 *
63	 * - `no_engine` — nothing has worked this number through the map yet.
64	 * - `no_market` — no venue quotes this claim.
65	 * - `not_said` — nobody has given a number. The one dash on screen with a
66	 *   meaning: the reader's own empty slot, inviting a number.
67	 * - `refused` — the engine was asked and **would not** work this number out. It
68	 *   is its own kind rather than a shade of `no_engine`, because the two are
69	 *   different facts: *nothing has run yet* invites waiting, and *the engine
70	 *   turned this down, here is why* invites repairing the thing it turned down.
71	 *   Reusing one word for both would make the reason on screen the only thing
72	 *   telling them apart, and a reason is not something code can read back.
73	 */
74	export type AbsenceKind = "no_engine" | "no_market" | "not_said" | "refused";
75	
76	/**
77	 * A number that is not here, and why.
78	 *
79	 * `words` is what the reader sees where the number would have been — "no
80	 * market", "no engine yet", "not worked out", or a dash. `reason` is the sentence
81	 * that says why, so no slot on screen is ever merely empty. `kind` is which of
82	 * the four this is, so that code can tell one absence from another without
83	 * reading its words back — the dash that invites a number is not the dash that
84	 * means nothing was computed.
85	 */
86	export interface Absence {
87	  /** Which absence this is. */
88	  readonly kind: AbsenceKind;
89	  /** What is printed where the number would be. Never blank, never a zero. */
90	  readonly words: string;
91	  /** Why there is no number, in plain words. */
92	  readonly reason: string;
93	}
94	
95	/**
96	 * A value we may not have, with the reason standing in its place when we do not.
97	 *
98	 * `reading` is optional — every number slot in this view model is — and when it
99	 * is missing, `absence` is present and says why. The two halves are written as
100	 * a choice between two shapes so that the type itself forbids an empty slot
101	 * with no reason attached: there is no way to write one down.
102	 */
103	export type Known<T> =
104	  | { readonly reading: T; readonly absence?: undefined }
105	  | { readonly reading?: undefined; readonly absence: Absence };
106	
107	/** The three voices on one claim, each in its own slot, never merged. */
108	export interface BeliefSlots {
109	  /** What the model thinks. */
110	  readonly model: Known<Ranged>;
111	  /** What the reader thinks. Absent until they say. */
112	  readonly user: Known<Ranged>;
113	  /** What a venue is pricing. Absent when no venue quotes this claim. */
114	  readonly market: Known<Ranged>;
115	}
116	
117	/**
118	 * What kind of push an arrow carries over time.
119	 *
120	 * `impulse` is a one-time spike that fades away by its own half-life. `step`
121	 * switches on and holds. `ramp` climbs from nothing to full size across the
122	 * delay and then holds. The wire's stroke pattern says which, and it is the
123	 * only thing the stroke says.
124	 */
125	export type LinkShape = "impulse" | "step" | "ramp";
126	
127	/**
128	 * Where an arrow and its number came from — a receipt our own pipeline writes,
129	 * never something a model says about itself.
130	 *
131	 * Seven values, drawn on the map as a mark of one, two or three dots at the
132	 * arrow's tail, with the exact word beside the same mark in the panel.
133	 */
134	export type Provenance =
135	  | "documented"
136	  | "historical"
137	  | "market_implied"
138	  | "argued"
139	  | "user"
140	  | "asserted"
141	  | "simulated";
142	
143	/** One published item behind an arrow, and the day we fetched it — or that nobody did. */
144	export interface SourceView {
145	  /** Where the reader goes to check it. */
146	  readonly url: string;
147	  /** What the reader will see when they get there, in the publisher's words. */
148	  readonly title: string;
149	  /** The host name the address points at, with any leading `www.` dropped. */
150	  readonly host: string;
151	  /** The day our own retrieval step fetched it, or the reason there is no day. */
152	  readonly retrieved: { readonly day: string } | { readonly absence: Absence };
153	}
154	
155	/** How often this kind of thing has happened before, when there is an honest set to count. */
156	export interface BaseRateView {
157	  /** The set of past cases being counted, stated so somebody else could recount them. */
158	  readonly referenceClass: string;
159	  /** How many cases in that set came out true. */
160	  readonly k: number;
161	  /** How many cases are in the set altogether. */
162	  readonly n: number;
163	  /** Web addresses where the count can be checked. Empty means nobody has checked it. */
164	  readonly sources: readonly SourceView[];
165	}
166	
167	/** One published item for or against a claim, as the tile shows it. */
168	export interface EvidenceClipping {
169	  /** What the source says, in one sentence, in our words. */
170	  readonly line: string;
171	  /**
172	   * A single letter standing for the publication, taken from the host name in
173	   * the source's own web address — `bbc.com` gives `B`.
174	   *
175	   * A letter rather than the publication's icon, on purpose: fetching an icon
176	   * is a request to somebody else's server, and the packaged demo draws its
177	   * first frame without making one.
178	   */
179	  readonly monogram: string;
180	  /** The host name the monogram came from, so the letter can be accounted for. */
181	  readonly host: string;
182	  /** `1` when the item supports the claim, `-1` when it cuts against it. */
183	  readonly direction: 1 | -1;
184	  /** Where to read it, so the reader can check us. */
185	  readonly url: string;
186	}
187	
188	/**
189	 * A word shown where a likelihood would go.
190	 *
191	 * While the reader has supposed a claim true it is true in every simulated
192	 * world, so there is no number to show and inventing one would answer a
193	 * question nobody asked. The tile shows *Supposed · Oct 1* instead. Nothing in
194	 * this pull request produces one — the buttons that do arrive later — but the
195	 * chip can already render it, and its test proves it.
196	 */
197	export interface Standing {
198	  /** The words, such as "Supposed · Oct 1". */
199	  readonly words: string;
200	  /** Why the claim stands this way, for the reader who asks. */
201	  readonly reason: string;
202	}
203	
204	/** One claim, as a tile draws it. */
205	export interface ClaimView {
206	  /** The claim's identifier on the map. */
207	  readonly id: string;
208	  /** The claim in one sentence, as a person would say it out loud. */
209	  readonly claim: string;
210	  /** What this claim is for. Carried on the tile by its shape. */
211	  readonly kind: ClaimKind;
212	  /** The day the claim is settled by, as the server wrote it: `2026-11-01`. */
213	  readonly resolvesBy: string;
214	  /** Who or what applies the test that settles it. */
215	  readonly resolutionSource: string;
216	  /**
217	   * The test itself, written so that two people reading it would agree on the
218	   * answer. Too long for a tile; the panel beside the map prints it in full.
219	   */
220	  readonly resolutionCriteria: string;
221	  /**
222	   * The model's likelihood for this claim before its causes are taken into
223	   * account. Never drawn on a tile — a second number beside the model's would
224	   * be a fourth voice — and always drawn in the panel, where the decomposition
225	   * starts from it.
226	   */
227	  readonly prior: Ranged;
228	  /** How often this kind of thing has happened before, or the reason there is no such count. */
229	  readonly baseRate: { readonly reading: BaseRateView } | { readonly absence: Absence };
230	  /** The three likelihoods, side by side. */
231	  readonly beliefs: BeliefSlots;
232	  /** At most two published items, for and against. What the tile has room for. */
233	  readonly evidence: readonly EvidenceClipping[];
234	  /**
235	   * Every published item on this claim, in the order the map stores them.
236	   *
237	   * The tile shows two; the panel shows all of them, because a claim you can
238	   * only see half the evidence for is a claim you cannot argue with.
239	   */
240	  readonly evidenceInFull: readonly EvidenceClipping[];
241	  /**
242	   * The multiplied-out likelihood of the steps of one route from the
243	   * hypothesis to this claim.
244	   *
245	   * A chain of four plausible steps is not a plausible chain, and this is the
246	   * number that says so. It arrives **on the world**, computed by the engine.
247	   * Nothing in the browser multiplies anything to fill it in, and the slot holds
248	   * its absence until the engine can answer.
249	   */
250	  readonly pathProduct: Known<Ranged>;
251	  /** A word shown instead of a likelihood, when the claim is standing on the reader's say-so. */
252	  readonly standing?: Standing;
253	  /**
254	   * What an edit did to this claim, in one word. Absent on a world with no
255	   * edits behind it — the base map, where nothing has been changed.
256	   */
257	  readonly diff?: DiffState;
258	  /**
259	   * How far this claim's likelihood moved, when the engine says it moved.
260	   *
261	   * Both numbers are the engine's, read on this claim's own resolve-by day, and
262	   * the browser subtracts nothing: which way it went is the engine's own word.
263	   * Absent on every claim the engine did not call `shifted`.
264	   */
265	  readonly moved?: Movement;
266	  /**
267	   * What this claim's tile says about the edits behind it, in order.
268	   *
269	   * Two badges in a row read as a sequence: *Supposed · Oct 1* then *Retracted
270	   * · Oct 2 · by "…"*. Empty on a claim no edit touched.
271	   */
272	  readonly badges?: readonly Badge[];
273	  /**
274	   * True when this claim is **not** in the world you are looking at.
275	   *
276	   * Two worlds are laid out once, together, and painted twice in the same
277	   * coordinates. A claim that only one of them has is still drawn in the other,
278	   * faint and dashed, so that flipping between them moves nothing and every
279	   * difference you see is a real difference rather than a re-layout.
280	   */
281	  readonly ghost?: boolean;
282	}
283	
284	/**
285	 * How far a claim's likelihood moved between two worlds, as the engine read it.
286	 *
287	 * Both numbers arrive from the engine at full precision and are printed as they
288	 * came. Which way it went is a word the engine's own reading decides, never a
289	 * subtraction done here — this half of the product does no arithmetic on the
290	 * map's numbers, and "is the second bigger than the first" would be the first
291	 * step down that road.
292	 */
293	export interface Movement {
294	  /** The first world's likelihood, on the claim's own resolve-by day. */
295	  readonly from: number;
296	  /** The second world's likelihood, on the same day. */
297	  readonly to: number;
298	  /** Which way it went. */
299	  readonly way: "up" | "down";
300	  /**
301	   * How far it moved, as the engine reported it.
302	   *
303	   * Carried beside the two readings because a move can be smaller than the
304	   * second significant figure: when the before and the after print the same,
305	   * this is the only thing that says anything moved at all.
306	   */
307	  readonly by: number;
308	  /**
309	   * The share of versions of the map that moved the same way. On screen this is
310	   * headed **same direction**; the word *agreement* is kept off the screen.
311	   */
312	  readonly sameDirection: Known<number>;
313	  /**
314	   * True when the engine says this claim moved **only** because an observation
315	   * made some versions of the map count for more than others.
316	   *
317	   * It comes from the engine's difference, on the claim's own row, and the
318	   * browser must never work it out for itself — whether a claim moved for that
319	   * reason is a fact about how the engine read the numbers, and only the engine
320	   * knows it. The panel prints one sentence when it is set.
321	   */
322	  readonly onlyReweighted?: boolean;
323	}
324	
325	/**
326	 * What an edit did to a claim.
327	 *
328	 * Four of the five are worked out from the branch alone, with no arithmetic
329	 * anywhere: following arrows is walking, not calculating.
330	 *
331	 * - `added` — the claim arrives in an **Add a claim** edit.
332	 * - `killed` — the claim is the target of a **Suppose this is false**. Forced
333	 *   false, full stop. "No path from the hypothesis reaches this any more" is a
334	 *   fact about a route, and the panel's path bar reports it in those words.
335	 * - `downstream` — the claim is in the affected set of at least one edit: a
336	 *   claim your change **can** move. Drawn live, its model number reading its
337	 *   absence, because nothing has worked the new number out.
338	 * - `untouched` — everything else. Identical to the base world, and the map can
339	 *   say so without hedging, because that is a proven property of an edit.
340	 * - `shifted` — the number moved, with a before and an after. It needs two
341	 *   numbers to compare, so only the engine ever produces one, and the browser
342	 *   copies the word across rather than deciding it.
343	 *
344	 * **Which of the two readings wins.** Once the engine has answered, its own word
345	 * is the authority wherever it has one — `added`, `killed` and `shifted` are
346	 * the engine's. `downstream` and `untouched` stay the browser's, because they
347	 * answer a different question: *can* your edit reach this claim, rather than
348	 * *did* its number move. A claim the edit can reach whose number did not move is
349	 * `downstream`, and saying `untouched` about it would be telling the reader
350	 * their change cannot reach something it can.
351	 */
352	export type DiffState = "added" | "killed" | "downstream" | "untouched" | "shifted";
353	
354	/**
355	 * One thing a tile says about an edit behind it — *Added*, *Supposed · Oct 1*,
356	 * *Retracted · Oct 2 · by "…"*.
357	 *
358	 * The words are copied from the shared vocabulary and never paraphrased, and
359	 * none of the six operations' code names ever appears in one.
360	 */
361	export interface Badge {
362	  /** The words on the badge. */
363	  readonly words: string;
364	  /** What the badge means, for the reader who asks. */
365	  readonly reason: string;
366	  /**
367	   * True when this badge says an earlier one no longer holds, so the tile can
368	   * draw the pair as a sequence with an arrow between them.
369	   */
370	  readonly overrides?: boolean;
371	  /**
372	   * True when this badge is how far the number moved — `.40 → .30 ▼` — rather
373	   * than a word about an edit.
374	   *
375	   * It sits with the badges because it is what the edits did to this claim, and
376	   * because the tile already reserves room for whatever they have to say. It is
377	   * drawn differently: the two readings in the number face with a chevron
378	   * between the old and the new.
379	   */
380	  readonly movement?: boolean;
381	}
382	
383	/** One arrow, as a wire draws it. */
384	export interface LinkView {
385	  /** The arrow's identifier: its two ends joined, such as `H->B`. */
386	  readonly id: string;
387	  /** The claim the arrow starts at. */
388	  readonly source: string;
389	  /** The claim the arrow ends at. */
390	  readonly target: string;
391	  /** Whether the push survives its cause going away. */
392	  readonly mode: LinkMode;
393	  /**
394	   * How hard this arrow pushes, signed, at full precision.
395	   *
396	   * It is signed **on the claim, not on the world**. The arrow into *Brent
397	   * settles below $68* is `+1.6` — positive, because it makes that claim come
398	   * out true more often — and the thing that claim describes is a *falling*
399	   * price. So a push's sign is not a direction of financial effect, it never
400	   * takes a direction hue, and it is carried by the printed sign and a word.
401	   *
402	   * Nothing on the canvas adds one of these to anything. Choosing a stroke
403	   * width or a word for it is a comparison against fixed thresholds.
404	   */
405	  readonly strength: number;
406	  /** Days from the cause becoming true to the push reaching full size. */
407	  readonly lag: number;
408	  /** What the push does over time. The wire's stroke pattern, and nothing else. */
409	  readonly shape: LinkShape;
410	  /** Days for an `impulse` push to fall to half its size. Absent on the other two shapes. */
411	  readonly halfLife: number | null;
412	  /** The mechanism in one to three plain sentences: why this cause moves this effect. */
413	  readonly rationale: string;
414	  /** What backs the arrow, each with the day it was fetched or the reason there is none. */
415	  readonly sources: readonly SourceView[];
416	  /** Where this arrow came from. Drawn as a mark at the tail, spelled out in the panel. */
417	  readonly provenance: Provenance;
418	  /**
419	   * The target's likelihood with this arrow's source supposed true.
420	   *
421	   * Not computed here and not carried on the world: it costs a whole extra
422	   * run of the map per arrow, so the engine works one out only when a wire is
423	   * asked about. Until then — and always, in this build, because that route
424	   * does not exist yet — the slot holds its absence and the wire's chip reads
425	   * the push back in words instead. Never a guessed number.
426	   */
427	  readonly conditional: Known<Ranged>;
428	  /**
429	   * True when this arrow is a market feeding back on the world. A feedback
430	   * arrow is the one arrow allowed to close a loop, and it is set aside when
431	   * the map is sorted into layers — otherwise there would be no left-to-right
432	   * order to sort it into.
433	   */
434	  readonly reflexive: boolean;
435	  /**
436	   * What an edit did to this arrow. Absent when no edit touched it.
437	   *
438	   * - `added` — an **Add a claim** edit brought it.
439	   * - `cut` — a supposition cut it: "take this as given, and do not tell me what
440	   *   caused it". It is still drawn, faint and dashed, because an arrow that
441	   *   simply vanished would be a change nobody could see.
442	   * - `retuned` — a **Change this push** edit moved its number.
443	   */
444	  readonly change?: "added" | "cut" | "retuned";
445	  /**
446	   * True when this arrow is **not** in the world you are looking at. Drawn faint
447	   * in the same place, so that flipping between the two worlds moves nothing.
448	   *
449	   * A ghost arrow is carried by how faint it is and by nothing else. Its stroke
450	   * is fully spent saying what kind of push it is — dot-dash for a spike that
451	   * fades, solid for a switch that holds, doubled when the push only lasts while
452	   * its cause does — and dashing it to say "other world" as well would leave it
453	   * saying neither clearly.
454	   */
455	  readonly ghost?: boolean;
456	}
457	
458	/**
459	 * One world: a map with its numbers as they stand.
460	 *
461	 * "As they stand" is doing real work. In this pull request the numbers are the
462	 * stored example's own, read from the fixture route. When the engine's world
463	 * route lands they will be computed, and the slots that read as absences today
464	 * will fill in. Nothing here has to change for that to happen, because nothing
465	 * false was written.
466	 */
467	export interface WorldView {
468	  /** Which stored example or map this world was built from. */
469	  readonly baseId: string;
470	  /** What the map is called on screen. */
471	  readonly title: string;
472	  /**
473	   * The day the map is set on, as the map itself writes it: `2026-10-01`.
474	   *
475	   * Every resolve-by date on the map is a span from this day, and an edit the
476	   * reader makes takes effect on it, so the map reads the same whenever it is
477	   * opened. The browser's own clock is never consulted: a supposition dated by
478	   * the reader's time zone would make the same map read differently in two
479	   * places.
480	   */
481	  readonly today: string;
482	  /**
483	   * The branch this world has applied, when it has one.
484	   *
485	   * Absent on the base world, which is the empty branch. What the branch panel
486	   * lists, and what every diff state on the claims above was worked out from.
487	   */
488	  readonly branch?: BranchView;
489	  /** The claim the reader started from. */
490	  readonly hypothesisId: string;
491	  /** Every claim on the map. */
492	  readonly claims: readonly ClaimView[];
493	  /** Every arrow on the map. */
494	  readonly links: readonly LinkView[];
495	  /**
496	   * How many versions of the map the engine ran to produce these numbers.
497	   *
498	   * Absent when nothing was computed — which is every world in this build,
499	   * because the engine's route does not exist yet. It is the one thing that
500	   * tells a belief chip whether its range was *computed* across many versions
501	   * of the map or merely *stated* by whoever wrote the number down, and the
502	   * chip says a different sentence for each. Nothing else reads it.
503	   */
504	  readonly versions?: number;
505	  /**
506	   * How many worlds ran under each version of the map: how the dice fall.
507	   *
508	   * Absent for the same reason `versions` is. It is printed in the sentence
509	   * under the map, beside the seed, so that a reader can rebuild this world.
510	   */
511	  readonly worldsPerVersion?: number;
512	  /**
513	   * The one number every random draw behind these likelihoods came from.
514	   *
515	   * A world is replayable from three things — the map, the branch and this — so
516	   * it is carried here and named under the map. Absent on a world nobody
517	   * computed.
518	   */
519	  readonly seed?: number;
520	  /**
521	   * Plain sentences the engine wanted the reader to see under the map.
522	   *
523	   * The engine writes these itself — for instance when so few worlds survived an
524	   * observation that the range around the answer stops meaning much. They are
525	   * printed as they came and never summarised.
526	   */
527	  readonly warnings?: readonly string[];
528	
529	  /**
530	   * Where these numbers came from, in one sentence a reader can check.
531	   *
532	   * It is printed under the map. A world whose numbers cannot say where they

1	/**
2	 * The world source that asks the engine, and draws the answers it gets back.
3	 *
4	 * This is where the two halves of the product meet. The canvas was written
5	 * against `WorldSource` and nothing else, so joining it to the engine changed no
6	 * component: the object handed in changed, the slots that used to read *no
7	 * engine yet* now hold computed numbers, and every absence that is still on
8	 * screen is still an absence for a reason it can name.
9	 *
10	 * **Three questions, three routes, and nothing else is asked.**
11	 *
12	 * | The question | Where it is asked |
13	 * |---|---|
14	 * | What does this branch make the map say? | `POST /api/worlds` |
15	 * | What moved between the map as written and the map with my edits? | `POST /api/worlds/diff` |
16	 * | What is the number on this one arrow? | `POST /api/worlds/conditional` |
17	 *
18	 * A fourth thing is read and is not the engine's: the map itself — the claims,
19	 * their wording, how each is judged, the arrows and what is cited for them —
20	 * which comes from the stored-example route. A map is written by hand; a world
21	 * never is. So the map is read once and kept, and the engine is asked again
22	 * every time an edit lands.
23	 *
24	 * **There is no arithmetic on a likelihood anywhere in this file.** Numbers
25	 * arrive from the engine and are carried, untouched and at full precision, to
26	 * the moment they are printed. Which way a claim moved is read off the sign of
27	 * the engine's own difference — a comparison, not a subtraction — and no two
28	 * numbers on this map are ever combined here.
29	 *
30	 * **Nothing here is invented.** A branch that does not fit comes back as every
31	 * reason at once and is thrown on for the screen to print. A claim under a live
32	 * supposition gets the word rather than the `1` the engine stores for it. And a
33	 * chain's multiplied-out likelihood, which the engine does not carry, stays an
34	 * absence that says exactly that rather than being worked out here.
35	 */
36	
37	import type { ClaimDiff, Diff, World } from "../api/client";
38	import { readConditional, readDiff, readExample, readWorld } from "../api/client";
39	import { ADDED, happened, retracted, supposed } from "../graph/diff/badges";
40	import { daysApart } from "../graph/diff/days";
41	import { filled, NO_PATH_PRODUCT, seedFor, toClaim, toLink } from "./fromTheServer";
42	import { NOT_ON_THIS_MAP } from "./naming";
43	import type { FixtureBundle, WorldSource } from "./source";
44	import type {
45	  Badge,
46	  BranchView,
47	  ClaimChange,
48	  ClaimView,
49	  ConditionalRequest,
50	  DeltaRow,
51	  DiffRequest,
52	  DiffView,
53	  Known,
54	  Movement,
55	  Ranged,
56	  Standing,
57	  WireBranch,
58	  WorldRequest,
59	  WorldView,
60	} from "./types";
61	
62	/**
63	 * Which likelihood on a claim's series is the one its tile shows.
64	 *
65	 * A tile's headline number is read on the claim's **own resolve-by day** — the
66	 * day the claim is judged, which every claim has and which the tile already
67	 * prints. So the word beside that number has to be read on the same day, or the
68	 * tile would say *Supposed* over a number worked out for a different morning.
69	 *
70	 * @param world The world as the engine built it.
71	 * @param resolvesBy The claim's own resolve-by day.
72	 * @returns Where that day sits among the days the world was worked through, or
73	 *   nothing at all when the day is outside the window or was not one of the days
74	 *   drawn.
75	 */
76	function whereItsDaySits(world: World, resolvesBy: string): number | null {
77	  const day = daysApart(world.day_zero, resolvesBy);
78	  if (day === null) {
79	    return null;
80	  }
81	  const at = world.series_days.indexOf(day);
82	  return at === -1 ? null : at;
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * What a tile says about the edits behind it, read off the world rather than
87	 * worked out from the branch.
88	 *
89	 * The world carries both halves: every value an edit fixed, in the order the
90	 * edits were made, and every supposition a later edit undermined with the day
91	 * and the arrow that did it. Reading the badges off those is what closes the
92	 * question the diff chapter left open — two derivations of one line eventually
93	 * disagree, so there is one, and it is the world's.
94	 *
95	 * One badge is not on the world and cannot be: **Added**. Whether a claim
96	 * arrived with an edit is a fact about the branch, and the branch is what says
97	 * so — the world only shows the map the edits left behind, in which an added
98	 * claim looks like any other.
99	 *
100	 * @param world The world as the engine built it.
101	 * @param words Every claim's own words, so a badge can quote one.
102	 * @param added The claims this branch brought with it.
103	 * @returns One list of badges per claim that has any, in the order they were
104	 *   earned.
105	 */
106	function badgesFromTheWorld(
107	  world: World,
108	  words: ReadonlyMap<string, string>,
109	  added: ReadonlySet<string>,
110	): Map<string, Badge[]> {
111	  const badges = new Map<string, Badge[]>();
112	  const add = (claim: string, badge: Badge): void => {
113	    badges.set(claim, [...(badges.get(claim) ?? []), badge]);
114	  };
115	
116	  // A claim an edit brought with it earns **Added** before anything it is later
117	  // supposed to be: it has to be on the map before anything can be said about
118	  // it, so that is the order the two badges read in.
119	  for (const claim of added) {
120	    add(claim, ADDED);
121	  }
122	
123	  const supposedOn = new Map<string, string>();
124	  for (const fixed of world.assignments) {
125	    const day = fixed.at ?? world.day_zero;
126	    if (fixed.kind === "do") {
127	      add(fixed.target, supposed(day, fixed.value));
128	      if (fixed.value) {
129	        supposedOn.set(fixed.target, day);
130	      }
131	    } else {
132	      add(fixed.target, happened(day));
133	    }
134	  }
135	
136	  for (const end of world.retractions) {
137	    const cause = words.get(end.by_claim) ?? end.by_claim;
138	    add(end.target, retracted(end.at, cause, supposedOn.get(end.target) ?? end.at));
139	  }
140	
141	  return badges;
142	}
143	
144	/**
145	 * Which claims an edit has fixed the value of, on their own judging day.
146	 *
147	 * **One rule, and it is not a rule about suppositions.** A claim whose value an
148	 * edit fixed is true — or false — in every version of the map, so the engine
149	 * stores a flat `1` or `0` for it, and **no surface but the path product prints
150	 * that number.** Every other reader writes the word where the likelihood would
151	 * go: *Supposed · Oct 1* where the reader took it as given, *Happened · Oct 1*
152	 * where they reported it as news. Answering either with a likelihood is a tool
153	 * arguing with the person using it — and `>.99` is that number wearing the
154	 * certainty guard's clothes.
155	 *
156	 * **The two are found in different places, and that is the engine's shape rather
157	 * than ours.** A supposition can be undermined by a later edit, so whether it
158	 * still holds is a fact about a *day*, and the world's `states` carry it — H
159	 * reads *supposed* on the first and *pushed* by the day it is judged. An
160	 * observation is news: nothing takes it back, it holds across the whole window,
161	 * and the world records it as an assignment rather than as a state.
162	 *
163	 * @param world The world as the engine built it.
164	 * @param claims The claims, so each one's resolve-by day can be found.
165	 * @param badges The badges, for the words and the sentence behind them.
166	 */
167	function standingFromTheWorld(
168	  world: World,
169	  claims: readonly ClaimView[],
170	  badges: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly Badge[]>,
171	): Map<string, Standing> {
172	  const observed = new Set(
173	    world.assignments.filter((fixed) => fixed.kind === "observe").map((fixed) => fixed.target),
174	  );
175	  const standing = new Map<string, Standing>();
176	  for (const claim of claims) {

239	/**
240	 * Turn one computed world into the world the canvas draws.
241	 *
242	 * **This is the only function that does it.** Both callers — the stored-example
243	 * source below and the reducer that folds a generation's stream — hand their
244	 * world through here, so a map that was fetched and a map that was watched being
245	 * built cannot say different things about the same claim.
246	 *
247	 * @param world The world as the engine built it.
248	 * @param from What this map is called and where it came from.
249	 * @param branch The branch that was folded, or nothing on the base world.
250	 */
251	export function toWorldView(world: World, from: WorldSummary, branch?: BranchView): WorldView {
252	  // The map the engine's edits left behind, which is the map to draw: a branch
253	  // that added a claim added it here too.
254	  const claims = world.graph.propositions.map(toClaim);
255	  const words = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim.claim]));
256	  const added = new Set(
257	    (branch?.edits ?? []).flatMap((edit) => (edit.op === "insert" ? [edit.claimId] : [])),
258	  );
259	  const badges = badgesFromTheWorld(world, words, added);
260	  const standing = standingFromTheWorld(world, claims, badges);
261	
262	  return {
263	    baseId: from.id,
264	    title: from.title,
265	    today: from.day,
266	    hypothesisId: world.graph.hypothesis_id,
267	    claims: claims.map((claim): ClaimView => {
268	      const computed = world.beliefs[claim.id];
269	      return {
270	        ...claim,
271	        // The engine's own answer for this claim, read on the day the claim is
272	        // judged. It replaces the likelihood the map was written with, and it
273	        // replaces nothing else: the reader's own number and a venue's price
274	        // are theirs.
275	        beliefs: {
276	          ...claim.beliefs,
277	          model: computed === undefined ? claim.beliefs.model : filled(computed),
278	        },
279	        badges: badges.get(claim.id) ?? [],
280	        standing: standing.get(claim.id),
281	        // A chain's multiplied-out likelihood is not on a world, so it stays an
282	        // absence that says so. Nothing here multiplies one.
283	        pathProduct: { absence: NO_PATH_PRODUCT },
284	      };
285	    }),
286	    links: world.graph.links.map(toLink),
287	    versions: world.versions,
288	    worldsPerVersion: world.worlds,
289	    seed: world.seed,
290	    warnings: world.warnings,
291	    origin: from.origin,

295	/**
296	 * How far one claim moved, as the engine read it.
297	 *
298	 * Every part of it is the engine's own: the two readings, the sign that says
299	 * which way it went, the share of versions that agreed, and whether the move
300	 * came from nothing but the observation changing how much each version counts.
301	 * Nothing here subtracts, compares two numbers, or works anything out.
302	 *
303	 * @param row The claim's own row of the engine's difference.
304	 */
305	function movement(row: ClaimDiff): Movement | undefined {
306	  const { before, after, delta, agreement } = row;
307	  if (before === null || after === null || delta === null) {
308	    return undefined;
309	  }
310	  return {
311	    from: before,
312	    to: after,
313	    // Which way it went is the sign of the engine's own difference. Reading a
314	    // sign is a comparison against nought, not a subtraction: nothing here works
315	    // out how far anything moved.
316	    way: delta < 0 ? "down" : "up",
317	    by: delta,
318	    sameDirection:
319	      agreement === null
320	        ? {
321	            absence: {
322	              kind: "no_engine",
323	              words: "—",
324	              reason:
325	                "Only one of the two worlds holds this claim, so there is no direction for the " +
326	                "versions of the map to have agreed or disagreed about.",
327	            },
328	          }
329	        : { reading: agreement },
330	    // A claim with no causes of its own can move under **This happened** without
331	    // anything pushing on it: the observation makes the versions of the map in
332	    // which it was likely count for more, and the average shifts. The engine
333	    // says when that is the whole story, and the panel prints one sentence when
334	    // it does. **The browser never works this out for itself** — it is a fact
335	    // about how the engine read the numbers, and only the engine knows it.
336	    onlyReweighted: row.moved_only_by_reweighting,
337	  };
338	}

340	/** Turn the engine's difference into what the rail and the tiles read. */
341	function toDiffView(difference: Diff, claims: readonly ClaimView[]): DiffView {
342	  const byId = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim]));
343	
344	  const changed = new Map<string, ClaimChange>();
345	  for (const [id, one] of Object.entries(difference.claims)) {
346	    changed.set(id, {
347	      state: one.state,
348	      moved: movement(one),
349	    });
350	  }
351	
352	  // The endings that moved, in the engine's own order, largest rank first.
353	  // Nothing here sorts, re-ranks or drops a row.
354	  const ranked: DeltaRow[] = difference.rows.map((row): DeltaRow => {
355	    const claim = byId.get(row.target);
356	    return {
357	      claimId: row.target,
358	      label: claim?.claim ?? NOT_ON_THIS_MAP,
359	      kind: claim?.kind ?? "market",
360	      move: {
361	        reading: {
362	          from: row.before,
363	          to: row.after,
364	          largestOn: row.at_day,
365	          way: row.peak_delta < 0 ? "down" : "up",
366	          by: row.peak_delta,
367	        },
368	      },
369	      rangeWidth: { reading: row.range_width },
370	      agreement: { reading: row.agreement },
371	    };
372	  });
373	
374	  // An ending the engine left off that list did not move. Silence cannot be
375	  // told from absence — a reader would not know whether the ending held still
376	  // or is simply not on this map — so it gets a quiet row of its own, after
377	  // every ranked row and never mixed in among them.
378	  const listed = new Set(ranked.map((row) => row.claimId));
379	  const held: DeltaRow[] = claims
380	    .filter(
381	      (claim) =>
382	        (claim.kind === "market" || claim.kind === "not_tradeable") &&
383	        !listed.has(claim.id) &&
384	        changed.get(claim.id)?.state === "unchanged",
385	    )
386	    .map((claim) => ({
387	      claimId: claim.id,
388	      label: claim.claim,
389	      kind: claim.kind,
390	      move: {
391	        absence: {
392	          kind: "no_engine" as const,
393	          words: "no change",
394	          reason:
395	            "This ending is on the map and your edit did not move it: the engine compared the " +
396	            "two worlds and found no move worth reporting. It is listed so that holding still " +
397	            "cannot be mistaken for not being here.",
398	        },
399	      },
400	      rangeWidth: {
401	        absence: {
402	          kind: "no_engine" as const,
403	          words: "—",
404	          reason: "How firm a number is only says something about a number that moved.",
405	        },
406	      },
407	      agreement: {
408	        absence: {
409	          kind: "no_engine" as const,
410	          words: "—",
411	          reason:
412	            "Whether the versions of the map agreed on a direction only says something about a " +
413	            "claim that had a direction.",
414	        },
415	      },
416	      noChange: true,
417	    }));
418	
419	  const summary: Known<string> = { reading: difference.summary };
420	  return { claims: changed, rows: [...ranked, ...held], summary, warnings: difference.warnings };
421	}

448	 * number on one arrow.

451	 * written by hand and does not change while the page is open. It keeps no

510	   */

512	    const bundle = await this.readBundle(request.baseId);
513	    const difference = await readDiff(request.baseId, sendable(request.branch), seedFor(bundle));

515	    // can name an ending rather than print its identifier.

519	    return toDiffView(difference, claims);

522	  /**

532	      seedFor(bundle),
533	      request.linkId,

90	/**
91	 * Read every reason out of a refusal, whatever shape the refusal took.
92	 *
93	 * Two different bodies arrive under the same number. A branch that does not fit
94	 * the map comes back as the server's own list — a rule, the thing at fault, and
95	 * a sentence naming the claim or the arrow by its words. A body the web
96	 * framework could not read at all comes back as *its* list, which has a field
97	 * path and a message instead. Both are reasons a person can act on, so both are
98	 * turned into the same three fields here, and neither is swallowed.
99	 *
100	 * @param body Whatever came back beside the refusal.
101	 * @returns Every reason, in the order they arrived. Never empty: a refusal with
102	 *   nothing in it still gets one sentence, because a screen that says "refused"
103	 *   and nothing else is worse than no screen at all.
104	 */
105	function everyReason(body: unknown): Violation[] {
106	  const listed = (body as { detail?: unknown } | null)?.detail;
107	  if (!Array.isArray(listed) || listed.length === 0) {
108	    return [
109	      {
110	        code: "edit_not_applicable",
111	        subject: "",
112	        message:
113	          "The server would not carry this out and did not say why. Nothing was changed on the map.",
114	      },
115	    ];
116	  }
117	  return listed.map((one): Violation => {
118	    const reason = one as Partial<Violation> & { msg?: string; loc?: readonly unknown[] };
119	    if (typeof reason.message === "string") {
120	      return {
121	        code: reason.code ?? "edit_not_applicable",
122	        subject: reason.subject ?? "",
123	        message: reason.message,
124	      };
125	    }
126	    // The framework's own shape: a path to the field it could not read, and a
127	    // sentence about it. The path is the nearest thing to a subject there is.
128	    const where = (reason.loc ?? []).map(String).join(" → ");
129	    return {
130	      code: "edit_not_applicable",
131	      subject: where,
132	      message:
133	        where === ""
134	          ? (reason.msg ?? "The server could not read this request.")
135	          : `The server could not read this request at ${where}: ${reason.msg ?? "no reason given"}.`,
136	    };
137	  });

145	 *   can see which of the three readings went wrong.
146	 * @param request The already-typed call to make.
147	 */
148	async function read<Reading>(
149	  address: string,
150	  request: () => Promise<{ data?: Reading; error?: unknown; response: Response }>,
151	): Promise<Reading> {
152	  let answer: { data?: Reading; error?: unknown; response: Response };
153	  try {
154	    answer = await request();
155	  } catch {
156	    throw new Error(`Could not reach the server at ${address}. It may not be running.`);
157	  }
158	  if (answer.data === undefined) {
159	    const numbered = answer.response.status;
160	    // A branch that does not fit the map is not a breakage: it is something the
161	    // reader can repair, and the server says every reason at once so that they
162	    // can repair all of it in one go. It comes back as its own kind of error so
163	    // that the screen can print the list rather than one sentence about it.
164	    if (numbered === 422) {
165	      throw new RefusedBranch(everyReason(answer.error));
166	    }
167	    // A web server that forwards requests on to another program replies with
168	    // 502, 503 or 504 when that program did not answer at all. In practice that
169	    // means the server is not running, so say so rather than repeating a number
170	    // the reader would have to look up.
171	    const reason =
172	      numbered === 502 || numbered === 503 || numbered === 504
173	        ? `Nothing answered at ${address} — the server may not be running.`
174	        : `The request to ${address} came back with no reading.`;
175	    throw new Error(`${reason} The reply was numbered ${numbered}.`);
176	  }
177	  return answer.data;
178	}

## 1. STATE MANAGEMENT

**Approach: plain `useState` + effects. No reducer, no context, no external store.**

```
grep -rn 'useReducer|createContext|useContext|zustand|redux|jotai' src → 0 hits
grep -rn 'React.memo|\bmemo\('                                       → 0 hits
```

`useState` census: `src/App.tsx` **25**, `src/components/BranchPanel.tsx` 8, `InputBar.tsx` 4, `AddAClaim.tsx` 4, `CommandPalette.tsx` 3, `Canvas.tsx` 2, `DeltaRail.tsx` 2, `BeliefChip.tsx` 2, `layoutRunner.ts` 2. `useEffect`: App.tsx 11, Canvas.tsx 5, everything else ≤2.

**Where world state lives.** Nowhere central. It is split across three places that must agree:

| Thing | Where | Line |
|---|---|---|
| Which screen + the fetched base world + branches | `screen` state in `App()` | `App.tsx:1294` |
| Which source answered | `using` state in `App()` | `App.tsx:1295` |
| Branches + which is open | `shop` state in `MapScreen` | `App.tsx:423` |
| Engine's answer for the open branch | `answer` state | `App.tsx:446` |
| Per-arrow conditional cache | `wireNumbers` state | `App.tsx:487` |
| Tile positions | `useLayout` state in a hook | `layoutRunner.ts:165` |

`MapScreen` alone holds `shop, showing, selection, focused, dock, onlyColumn, overlay, intervening, naming, status, arriving, answer, wireNumbers` — 13 `useState` + 4 `useRef` (`App.tsx:423–487`, `439`, `346–348` in Canvas).

**The tile-edit → re-render path** (this is the interesting one):

1. Button in `InterventionPanel` → `onEdit` → `edit()` (`App.tsx:634–638`) → `setShop(appendEdit(...))`.
2. `appendEdit` (`world/branchReducer.ts:172`) returns a brand-new `Workshop` with a new branch object.
3. `open` (`App.tsx:441`) is now a different object → the effect at `App.tsx:447–479` fires (deps `[source, base.baseId, open]`) → `setAnswer({at:"asking"})` → two POSTs.
4. Answer lands → `setAnswer({at:"answered", ...})` → `bothPaintings()` (`graph/diff/branchWorld.ts:301`) builds *both* worlds → `toFlow` → `useLayout` → ELK → positions → `planRoutes` + `planPlates` → render.

That is a genuinely well-thought-out unidirectional flow. **But it is broken by a memoization defect** (see §7, item 1).

**Prop drilling: yes, moderate.** `world` is threaded to `MapCanvas`, `InterventionPanel`, `BranchPanel`, `Inspector` (`App.tsx:797, 844, 853, 869`) and then again from `Inspector` down to `ClaimDetail`/`WireDetail`/`PathBar` (`Inspector.tsx:425, 537`, `PathBar.tsx:217`). `MapCanvas` takes **13 props** (`Canvas.tsx:94–165`). `selection`/`focused`/`onSelect`/`onFocused` are drilled as four separate props through two levels. A single `MapContext` or a `useReducer` over `{selection, focused, dock, overlay, status}` would delete ~30 lines of plumbing. It is not egregious — the tree is only 2–3 deep — but `MapScreen` is doing the job of a store.

**Derived-state-in-state bugs:**

- **`App.tsx:423`** — `useState(() => workshopOf(branches))`. Props copied into state, and the `branches` prop is never reconciled afterwards. This is only safe by accident: `App` unmounts `MapScreen` while `screen.at === "opening"` (`App.tsx:1374`), so a new map always remounts. There is no `key` on `<MapScreen>` (`App.tsx:1364`) making that guarantee explicit. One refactor away from a stale-branches bug.
- **`App.tsx:481`** — `const engine = engineState(answer)` — a derived value recomputed unmemoized in the render body that returns **a fresh object literal every time** (`engineState`, `App.tsx:347–360`). It is then a dependency of `useMemo` at `App.tsx:488–491`. This defeats every downstream memo in the file. Detailed in §7.
- **`App.tsx:594`** — the conditional-fetch effect lists `wireNumbers` (the state it writes) in its own deps. It is saved by the `.has(key)` guard at `:570`, but it is the classic re-entrant-effect shape.
- **`App.tsx:1040–1051`** — `seenSoFar` ref vs `growth.world.claims.length` as an arrival detector. Monotonic-counter-in-a-ref: if the claim count ever *shrinks* and regrows (the engine's world replaces the drafted one at `stream/growth.ts:330`), arrivals are silently missed. The comment at `:1034–1039` shows they thought about it; the mechanism is still fragile.

**Single source of truth?** For the *data*, yes and it's good: `WorldView` is the one shape everything draws, and `toWorldView` (`world/apiSource.ts:251`) is explicitly the only function that produces one — with a comment saying why (`:241–246`). For the *UI*, no: `screen` (`App.tsx:1294`) and `using` (`:1295`) are two states that must agree about which source produced the map on screen, set in two separate branches (`:1311–1313` vs `:1320–1327`).

---

## 2. DUPLICATION — `world/types.ts` vs `api/schema.ts`

**Verdict: it is a *view model*, not a mirror — but the boundary is leakier than the file's own 27-line defence admits.**

`world/types.ts:1–27` opens by arguing it is deliberately *not* generated. Then `types.ts:29` imports `components` from the schema anyway, and uses it three times: `WireBranch = components["schemas"]["Branch"]` (`:756`), `WireEdit = ...["Branch"]["interventions"][number]` (`:759`), and `drafted?: components["schemas"]["Insert"]` (`:686`). `world/source.ts:34` does the same for `FixtureBundle`. So the "hand-written" rule already has four exceptions.

**Concrete field-level overlap.** `LinkView` (`types.ts:384–456`) vs schema `Link` (`schema.ts:965–1031`):

| `LinkView` | schema `Link` |
|---|---|
| `id, source, target` | `id, source, target` |
| `mode: "trigger"\|"sustain"` | `mode: "trigger"\|"sustain"` |
| `strength, lag` | `strength, lag` |
| `shape: "impulse"\|"step"\|"ramp"` | `shape: "impulse"\|"step"\|"ramp"` |
| `halfLife: number\|null` | `half_life?: number\|null` |
| `rationale, sources, provenance, reflexive` | `rationale, sources, provenance, reflexive` |
| + `conditional`, `change?`, `ghost?` | — |

Twelve of fifteen fields are identical modulo camelCase. The three literal unions (`LinkMode` `types.ts:39`, `LinkShape` `:125`, `Provenance` `:134–141`) are hand-retyped copies of unions the generator already emits at `schema.ts:986, 1002, 1024`. Same for `ClaimKind` (`types.ts:32`) vs `schema.ts:1116`.

**Name collisions across the two files** — same identifier, different shape:

| Name | `world/types.ts` | `api/schema.ts` |
|---|---|---|
| `DeltaRow` | `:769` `{claimId, label, kind, move, rangeWidth, agreement, noChange}` | `:612` `{target, before, after, peak_delta, at_day, range_width, agreement, rank}` |
| `DiffRequest` | `:554` `{baseId, branch}` | `:728` `{base_id, branch_a, branch_b, seed, versions, worlds}` |
| `WorldRequest` | `:546` `{baseId, branch}` | `:1497` `{base_id, branch, seed, versions, worlds}` |
| `ConditionalRequest` | `:568` | `:528` |

`world/apiSource.ts:37–60` imports **both sets** into one module — `ClaimDiff, Diff, World` from the client, `DeltaRow, DiffRequest, ConditionalRequest, WorldRequest` from types. A reader has to hold two meanings of `DeltaRow` in their head at `apiSource.ts:354`. That is a real cost.

**Is there an adapter layer? Yes, and it is good.** `world/fromTheServer.ts` (292 lines) is the single conversion point — `toClaim` (`:212`), `toLink` (`:262`), `filled`/`missing` (`:65`, `:71`), `source` (`:118`), `baseRate` (`:148`). `apiSource.ts:251 toWorldView` is explicitly documented as the only world-shaped conversion, with the drift argument spelled out (`:241–246`). `world/index.ts` is a clean barrel and components never import `api/schema` directly (verified: only `client.ts`, `source.ts`, `types.ts`, `fromTheServer.ts`, `fixtureSource.ts`, `stream/events.ts`, `stream/insert.ts` touch it).

**Drift risk, honestly assessed.** Low-to-moderate, and structurally contained: the conversion functions are typed against generated inputs, so a server rename breaks `tsc` at `fromTheServer.ts` rather than at runtime. What *does* drift silently is the hand-copied literal unions — if the server adds an eighth `provenance` value, `schema.ts` grows it, `types.ts:134` does not, `toLink` at `fromTheServer.ts:275` still compiles (assignment to a narrower union... actually it would fail; good), but `encodings.ts:355 ORIGIN_STEPS: Record<Provenance, OriginStep>` would silently not cover it. Cost: **~250 of the 819 lines of `types.ts` are restatement**; the other ~570 are prose (see §6). The genuinely load-bearing invention — `Known<T>` / `Absence` (`types.ts:86–105`) — is excellent and has no schema equivalent.

---

## 3. `fixtureSource` vs `ApiWorldSource`

**The port.** `world/source.ts:39–65` — `interface WorldSource` with four methods: `readBundle`, `readWorld`, `readDiff`, `readConditional`. Genuinely clean, documented with *why* the seam exists (`source.ts:8–15`: two teams, routes not yet written).

**Two implementations:**
- `world/apiSource.ts:455 class ApiWorldSource implements WorldSource` — three POSTs, plus a private `#maps` promise-cache (`:457`) with correct failure eviction (`:469–474`).
- `world/fixtureSource.ts:151 class FixtureWorldSource implements WorldSource` — reads `/api/fixtures/{id}`; `readDiff` and `readConditional` **throw a prose sentence** rather than fake a number (`:187`, `:198`, via `noEngineHere` at `:130`). That is an unusually principled fallback.

**How the fixture mode is wired.**

```
grep -rn 'import.meta.env|VITE_|URLSearchParams|location.search' src e2e index.html → (none)
```

There is **no env var, no URL param, no runtime toggle**. Wiring is entirely by:
1. Module-level singletons: `App.tsx:1248 DEFAULT_SOURCE = new ApiWorldSource()`, `App.tsx:1258 FALLBACK_SOURCE = new FixtureWorldSource()`.
2. Props with defaults: `AppProps` (`App.tsx:1274–1281`), consumed at `App.tsx:1284–1288`.
3. **Automatic failover at runtime**: `open()` (`App.tsx:1297–1337`) tries `source`, and on rejection retries with `fallback` (`:1319`), then records which one won in `setUsing` (`:1321`) and prints a sentence under the map explaining the numbers are not computed (`insteadOfTheEngine`, `App.tsx:1265`). Double failure → one sentence, no blank screen (`:1331`).

**Assessment.** The port is the best-designed thing in the frontend. Two criticisms: (a) the fallback is *only* reachable by a real network failure — there is no way for a reviewer or a demo to force it, which means the `FixtureWorldSource` path is exercised by exactly zero tests (`grep FixtureWorldSource src` returns only `App.tsx` and `world/index.ts`); (b) the props-with-defaults injection is used by `App.test.tsx` only, so in production the injection point is dead configuration.

---

## 4. `src/graph/wires/` — what the ~1,900 lines do

Actual counts: **1,906 TS/TSX + 266 CSS = 2,172**, plus **1,272 lines of tests** in `wires/__tests__/`.

| File | Lines | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `route.ts` | 460 | Orthogonal routing. `roundedPath` (`:76`) corner-cutting SVG path builder; `tailOffsets` (`:152`) de-collides provenance marks at a shared socket; `merged` (`:168`) interval merge; `freeCorridor` (`:196`) / `freeBand` (`:234`) find a clear horizontal lane; `planRoutes` (`:283`) whole-map pass assigning each wire `direct` \| `corridor` \| `sky`; `corridorCorners` (`:390`) / `skyCorners` (`:417`); `longestRunMidpoint` (`:444`) label anchor. |
| `encodings.ts` | 414 | The visual grammar dictionary. `likelihoodStep` (`:60`) 5-step brightness ramp; `widthFor` (`:121`) 4 stroke widths from `\|strength\|`; `pushInWords` (`:172`) 5 word bands; `strokeFor` (`:276`) dash pattern per `LinkShape`; `modeInWords`, `lagInWords`, `originStep` (`:377`) 1–3 dots per provenance, `originInWords` (`:412`). **Pure lookup tables and threshold comparisons — no arithmetic on likelihoods**, which is enforced by a test (`__tests__/noArithmetic.test.ts`). |
| `plates.ts` | 383 | Label placement + collision avoidance. `socketsFor` (`:80`); `plateSize` (`:149`) estimates the label box from **character counts** (`INTERFACE_CHARACTER = 6.4`, `MONO_CHARACTER = 7.9`, `:113–114`); `spotsFor` (`:246`) generates ~37 candidate positions per wire; `planPlates` (`:334`) greedy first-fit against tiles, tail marks and already-placed plates. |
| `CausalWire.tsx` | 388 | The edge component. Picks the path (`:274–293`), double-strokes `sustain` wires to fake a parallel-line stroke (`:298–304`, `:357–365`), decides plate anchoring for short drops (`:323–340`). |
| `WireChip.tsx` | 114 | The label content itself. |
| `lens.ts` | 107 | `onThePathFrom` (`:80`) — ancestor+descendant BFS for the hover dim. |
| `WireMarks.tsx` | 40 | One `<defs>` arrowhead. |

**So: ~55% routing/geometry/collision, ~22% encoding lookup tables, ~20% the component, ~2% graph walk.**

**Is it proportionate?** Mostly yes, with one exception.

- `route.ts` is **justified**. The file header (`:10–26`) names the specific failure — an arrow skipping a column vanishes behind the intervening tile, so the picture asserts the opposite of the map. That is a correctness bug in a causal-diagram tool, not a polish item. 460 lines for a corridor-finder with interval merging is normal.
- `encodings.ts` at 414 lines is **57% comment** (235/414) for 146 lines of actual lookup tables. The *content* is ~140 lines of `Record<>` literals. Proportionate as code, bloated as a file.
- **`plates.ts` is the one that is not proportionate.** 383 lines of greedy collision avoidance whose input is a *character-count estimate* of the label box (`:113–127`). The whole sub-system exists because "the union crowds the middle of the map and plates began landing on one another" (`Canvas.tsx:291–294`). A measured-DOM approach, or simply putting the reading in the Inspector only, would delete all 383 lines plus the `plateAt`/`plateAnchor`/`ridesAside`/`asideBelow` branching in `CausalWire.tsx:323–345`. And it runs on every render (§7).

`world/types.ts` is 569 comment lines for 213 lines of type declarations — a 2.7:1 ratio. The prose is *unusually high quality* — it explains rationale and rejected alternatives, not mechanics. But at this density it has two costs a reviewer should name:

1. **It is unverifiable.** `App.tsx:592` in Canvas has a 1-line `biome-ignore` justification; `types.ts:326–336` has a 10-line explanation of a field whose invariant nothing checks. The comments assert invariants; only `noArithmetic.test.ts` and `colourLaw.test.ts` actually enforce any of them.
2. **It hides the outliers.** `App.tsx` is 1,438 lines at only 20% comment — meaning **1,064 lines of actual code in one file** — and that fact is easy to miss when the codebase average is 39%.

---

## 7. PERFORMANCE

**1. The headline defect: every memo in `MapScreen` is defeated on every render.**

```
App.tsx:347  function engineState(answer: Answered): Engine | undefined {
App.tsx:350    return { at: "answered", now: ..., change: ... };   // fresh object
App.tsx:352    return { at: "waiting", absence: WHILE_ASKING };    // fresh object
...
App.tsx:481  const engine = engineState(answer);                   // NOT memoized
App.tsx:488  const paintings = useMemo(
App.tsx:489    () => (open === undefined ? null : bothPaintings(base, open, engine)),
App.tsx:491    [base, open, engine],                               // ← new identity every render
App.tsx:491  );
```

`engine` is a fresh object literal on every render, so `paintings` recomputes every render. That cascades:

- `paintings` → `bothPaintings` (`graph/diff/branchWorld.ts:301`) builds **two** full `WorldView`s, runs reachability (`diff/reach.ts`), badges, standings.
- `painted` (`:493`) → `world` `useMemo` (`:504–515`) → new object.
- `heights` `useMemo` (`:523–534`, deps `[paintings]`) → recomputes, calling `roomFor` per claim, which calls `tileHeight` **three times per claim** (`App.tsx:387–389`).
- `rows` (`:539`), `outline` (`:548`), `announcement` (`:555`), `keys` (`:640`, deps `[paintings]`) → all recompute; `keys` gets a new identity → `MapCanvas` re-renders.
- Inside `MapCanvas`: `drawing = useMemo(toFlow, [world, heights, reserved])` (`Canvas.tsx:188`) recomputes; `boxes` (`:205`), `nodes` (`:248`), and critically **`edges` (`:278–327`) which calls `planRoutes` + `tailOffsets` + `planPlates`**.

**Trigger:** anything that sets state in `MapScreen`. `setStatus` fires on **every keystroke** (`useMapKeys` → `onStatus`, `Canvas.tsx:584`). So pressing `j` re-runs full wire routing and plate collision avoidance for the whole map.

`planPlates` (`plates.ts:334–382`) is O(W × 37 × (T + 2W)) — for 60 tiles / 80 wires that is ~650k rect intersections per keystroke.

**Fix is one line:** `const engine = useMemo(() => engineState(answer), [answer]);`

**2. The `edges` memo depends on `lens`, so hover re-routes the map.**

`Canvas.tsx:327` deps are `[drawing, boxes, lens, selection, tooSmallForWords, world, column]`. `lens` changes on every `onNodeMouseEnter`/`Leave` (`:678–679`). Routing and plate placement do not depend on the lens — only `data.dimmed` (`:322`) does. Moving mouse across the map re-runs `planRoutes`+`planPlates` per tile crossed. This is a structural problem independent of defect 1.

**3. O(n²) height lookup.**

```
Canvas.tsx:199  const heightOf = useCallback(
Canvas.tsx:200    (id) => drawing.tiles.find((tile) => tile.id === id)?.height ?? 0, [drawing]);
```
Linear `find` called inside loops at `:208` (per position), `:341` (per position), `:549` (per position), plus `:421`, `:427`. Should be a `Map`.

**4. Layout: yes, it is on a worker — and this part is genuinely well done.**

`graph/layoutRunner.ts:24–25` loads elkjs's own worker script via `?url` and hands it to `new ELK({ workerUrl })` (`:73`). The header (`:1–22`) explains why wrapping it in a custom Worker fails. There is a 2-second `THREAD_PATIENCE` fallback (`:89`) that dynamically imports `elk.bundled.js` and lays out on the main thread (`:112–113`) — correct defensive design for browsers that block the worker.

**Is layout re-run on every interaction? No — and the guard is good.** `useLayout` memoizes on a `JSON.stringify` of `[[id,height],[id,source,target]]` (`:149–156`), so identity churn in the `tiles`/`edges` arrays does not trigger a re-layout. Pinning (`elkGraph.ts:64 pinsFor`) keeps already-placed tiles still as a map grows.

Two complaints about it:
- **`layoutRunner.ts:181`** — the effect then does `JSON.parse(shape)` to rebuild the arrays it already had in scope. Stringify-as-memo-key is a known hack; stringify-*and-parse-back* as the data path is worse. Use a `useMemo` producing the arrays plus a separate key.
- **`layoutRunner.ts:103–108`** — the `setTimeout` inside `Promise.race` is never cleared. Every layout run leaks a pending 2-second timer holding a closure. Under `StrictMode` (`main.tsx:27`) effects run twice, so two per layout.

**5. `useMemo`/`useCallback`: under-used where it matters, absent everywhere else.**

Only `App.tsx` (20 uses) and `Canvas.tsx` (16) memoize at all. Zero `React.memo` in the codebase. `Inspector` (826 lines), `BranchPanel` (566), `Tile` (342), `DeltaRail`, `PathBar` all re-render unconditionally on every `MapScreen` state change. Because `world` is a new object every render (defect 1), they would re-render even *with* `React.memo`. `Tile` is rendered once per claim and does `find`s internally (`Tile.tsx:142`), and `Inspector` does 2 linear `find`s per render (`:798, :800`) plus 2 more in `WireDetail` (`:538–539`).

**6. Minor:** `App.tsx:487` `useState<...>(new Map())` — non-lazy initializer allocates a Map every render. `Canvas.tsx:685` `proOptions={{...}}` and `:688` `defaultEdgeOptions={{...}}` are fresh object props each render. `App.tsx:806` `onOverflow={(column) => {...}}` inline. `Canvas.tsx:561–564 onTheGlass` does a `querySelectorAll` + array scan on every keyboard move.

---

## 8. THINGS A SENIOR REVIEWER WOULD WINCE AT

1. **`App.tsx` is 1,438 lines** containing three screen components (`MapScreen` `:408`, `GenerationScreen` `:979`, `App` `:1284`), two custom hooks (`useAnswer` `:119`, `useGeneration` `:923`), three `Absence` constants, four `Reading` formatters, and `roomFor`. It should be five files.
2. **`App.tsx:481` + `:488–491`** — unmemoized fresh-object dependency defeating the entire derived chain. See §7.1. This is the single highest-value fix in the repo.
3. **`Canvas.tsx:327`** — `edges` memo (full routing + plate collision) keyed on `lens`, so hover re-routes the map.
4. **`Canvas.tsx:199–202`** — O(n) `find` used as an O(1) lookup, called O(n) times in four places.
5. **`layoutRunner.ts:103–108`** — uncancelled `setTimeout` in a `Promise.race`; leaks a timer per layout, doubled by StrictMode.
6. **`layoutRunner.ts:149–156` → `:181`** — `JSON.stringify` then `JSON.parse` round-trip as both memo key and data channel.
7. **Text metrics hardcoded as character counts.** `geometry.ts:107 BADGE_CHARACTERS_PER_LINE = 38`, `:125 CLAIM_CHARACTERS_PER_LINE = 33`, `:64 CLAIM_LINE = 20.25`, `plates.ts:113 INTERFACE_CHARACTER = 6.4`, `:114 MONO_CHARACTER = 7.9`. Tile heights and plate boxes are *predicted* rather than measured. This breaks silently on a browser font-size override, during the webfont swap, or with any non-Latin text. ## THINGS THAT ARE GENUINELY EXCELLENT

1. **`Known<T>` / `Absence` (`world/types.ts:86–105`).** A discriminated union that makes "a missing number with no reason" *unrepresentable*: `{reading: T, absence?: undefined} | {reading?: undefined, absence: Absence}`. Four absence kinds (`:74`) so code can distinguish them without string-matching prose. This is the best type in the codebase and it is threaded consistently through every number slot.
2. **`WorldSource` (`world/source.ts:39–65`).** A 4-method port with two implementations and a documented rationale. Textbook.
3. **`toWorldView` as the single conversion (`world/apiSource.ts:251`).** Explicitly documented as the *only* function producing a `WorldView` (`:241–246`), used by both the fetch path and the streaming path (`stream/growth.ts`), so a fetched map and a watched-being-built map cannot disagree.
4. **The architectural tests.** These are rare and impressive:
   - `graph/wires/__tests__/noArithmetic.test.ts` — walks the **TypeScript AST** of listed files to prove no multiplication/addition touches a likelihood.
   - `styles/__tests__/colourLaw.test.ts` — parses every `.css` file and enforces "one channel per meaning"; asserts only four named files may use the likelihood ramp tokens.
   - `styles/__tests__/motionBudget.test.ts` — enforces that every duration in the product is one of three named tokens.
   - `graph/wires/__tests__/strokeIsShapeOnly.test.tsx`, `notByColourAlone.test.tsx` — accessibility invariants as unit tests.
   - `scripts/no-library-stylesheet.mjs` — a build-failing check that @xyflow's full stylesheet never enters the tree, including via CSS `@import` (which a linter cannot see).
5. **Layout on a real worker, with a main-thread fallback and a documented dead end** (`layoutRunner.ts:1–22, 89–114`).
6. **Race cancellation done correctly and consistently.** `stillOnScreen`/`stillWanted` flags in every async effect: `App.tsx:123–138`, `:452–474`, `:573–593`, `:1013–1022`, `:926–962`, `layoutRunner.ts:173–217`. With the correct reasoning written down at `App.tsx:470–473`.
7. **`branchReducer.ts` — append-only branches.** `appendEdit` (`:172`) keeps prior edits as *the same objects* so "nothing was rewritten" is checkable by identity; the dual representation (drawable + wire) is mutated in exactly one function so the two cannot diverge (`:165–170`). `workshopOf`/`openBranch`/`forkBranch` are pure.
8. **`api/client.ts:66–82 RefusedBranch`** — a typed error carrying *every* validation reason, with the argument for why (`:58–61`: "a person fixing a branch one fault per attempt learns only that the tool is hostile"). `everyReason` (`:105`) normalizes FastAPI's shape and the app's own shape into one. 502/503/504 translated into "the server may not be running" (`:171–174`) rather than echoing a status code.
9. **Graceful degradation as a first-class path** (`App.tsx:1297–1337`) — engine fails → stored example + a sentence saying these numbers are illustrative, not computed. Never a blank screen, never a fake number.
10. **TypeScript config is maximally strict** (`tsconfig.app.json`): `strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitOverride`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`. Zero `any`, zero `@ts-ignore`, zero non-null assertions, zero `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the whole tree.
11. **Every `biome-ignore` carries a real justification** (8 of them, e.g. `Canvas.tsx:592`, `BranchPanel.tsx:233`, `fixtureSource.ts:75`). None are bare suppressions.
12. **Accessibility is designed, not retrofitted.** A parallel text rendering of the whole graph (`a11y/sentences.ts:238 outlineOf`, `claimSentence:166`), polite live regions with staged announcements (`App.tsx:879`, `:1216`, reasoning at `:551–558`), a full keyboard map bound once on the page with a documented table (`keyboard/useMapKeys.ts:1–30`), and the primary e2e test performed **entirely by keyboard** (`e2e/hormuz.spec.ts:98`).
13. **Comment quality** (density aside). These explain *rejected alternatives* — `Canvas.tsx:526–534` (why landing on a wire doesn't select it), `App.tsx:619–625` (why the settle timer needs its own effect), `layoutRunner.ts:14–18` (why a custom worker wrapper fails). That is the kind of comment that survives refactors.
